tagline: A long gravel loop from Surprise Valley into Nevada and back.
intro: From the four-way stop in Cedarville the loop heads east across Surprise Valley, past the Alkali Lakes, which flood shallow in winter and spring and dry up most summers, and over the state line into Nevada. It swings north through sagebrush uplands and the old homestead country of Long Valley, then comes back west to Fort Bidwell and down the valley under the Warner Mountains. Parts are paved, parts are improved gravel, and some sections are dirt.

The valley was named in 1860 by Captain Alanson Nightingill, who insisted it be called after his first impression of it. Contrary to local lore, and to earlier editions of the BLM's own booklet, the emigrants had nothing to do with it.

moments.title: Fortynine Rock
moments.text: On the Applegate-Lassen Trail of 1849, the first 49 on this rock is said to be daubed in wagon axle grease, marking the last camp with good water before the dry valley floor.

moments.title: Mosquito Lake
moments.text: The road crosses Mosquito Lake on a levee, and when there is water in spring and early summer the shorebirds come, a black-and-white flock among them being willets.

moments.title: Fort Bidwell
moments.text: The old cavalry post at the north end of the valley later became an Indian school and hospital, and the stone general store, built in 1874, last sold gas at 89 cents a gallon.

practical: Dirt sections may need high ground clearance and possibly four-wheel drive, and the road west out of Mosquito Valley is narrow, fairly steep and not recommended for long trailers or long motor homes. Outside Cedarville and Fort Bidwell there are no services, and there is typically no cell phone service east of the state line.
